answers.answer: Starting hands are 4 cards each for 2 players, 3 each for 3 players, and 2 each for 4 players. Remove/set aside Epidemic cards before shuffling and dealing the remaining City and Event cards. Place each player pawn in Atlanta.
answers.evidence: Setup: “Remove Epidemic cards and set aside”; starting-hands table; “Place matching colored pawns in Atlanta.”

answers.answer: Put the Infection Rate marker on the leftmost 2 space. Flip 3 Infection cards and place 3 matching-color cubes on each named city; flip 3 more and place 2 cubes on each; flip 3 more and place 1 cube on each. Put all 9 revealed Infection cards face up on the Infection Discard Pile. The remaining Infection cards form the Infection Deck.
answers.evidence: Setup, “Infect initial cities”: leftmost “2”; 3 cards at 3 cubes, 3 at 2, 3 at 1; 9 face up in discard; rest form deck.

answers.answer: Use 4 Epidemics for Introductory, 5 for Standard, or 6 for Heroic; remove unused Epidemic cards. Divide the remaining Player cards into that many face-down piles, as equal in size as possible; shuffle one Epidemic into each pile face down; stack the piles into the Player Deck with smaller piles on the bottom.
answers.evidence: Setup, “Prepare the Player Deck”: difficulty counts, remove unused cards, piles equal in number to Epidemics and as equal in size as possible; smaller piles on bottom.

answers.answer: Take up to 4 actions; you may repeat an action, with each repetition costing another action, or stop early. Discard cards paid for action costs to the Player Discard Pile. Then draw 2 Player cards together, resolve any Epidemics first, and discard or play Events until within the 7-card limit; then infect cities by flipping cards equal to the current infection rate. After all three phases, play passes to the left.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure and Actions; all action-cost discards go to the Player Discard Pile; phases in order; turn passes left.

answers.answer: Drive/Ferry: move to a city connected by a white line, with no card cost. Direct Flight: discard the City card naming the destination. Charter Flight: discard the City card matching your current city to move to any city. Shuttle Flight: move from a city with a research station to any other city with a research station. White lines going off one board edge wrap to the other edge, so those cities are connected.
answers.evidence: Movement Actions table; Special Rules, “Board wrapping”: white lines off one edge wrap to the other (example: Sydney and Los Angeles).

answers.answer: Normally, spend one action, discard the City card matching your current city, take a research station from the supply, and place it in your current city. If all six stations are already built, relocate one from anywhere on the board. Any supplied extras beyond six are set aside during setup.
answers.evidence: Other Actions, “Build a Research Station”; Special Rules: only 6 exist and relocate one if all are placed; set extras aside during setup.

answers.answer: One Treat Disease action removes 1 cube of one chosen color if that disease is uncured. If it is cured, that action removes all cubes of that one color from the city. The other colors require separate Treat Disease actions, following the same rule for each color. Return removed cubes to the cube supply.
answers.evidence: Actions, “Treat Disease”: 1 cube, or all of one color if cured; each different color takes a separate action; cubes return to supply.

answers.answer: At any research station, discard 5 City cards of the disease color (4 if the player is the Scientist); the station city need not match that color. Move that disease’s cure marker to its Cure Indicator. Existing cubes remain, and the disease can still infect during normal infections and Epidemics until eradicated. If no cubes of that color are on the board when the cure is discovered, eradicate it immediately and flip its marker.
answers.evidence: Cure Procedure and Discover a Cure action; 5 cards/4 for Scientist; any station; existing cubes remain; no cubes means immediate eradication and flip.

answers.answer: Either give the City card matching the city both players occupy to the other player, or take that matching card from them. Both players must agree. If the recipient reaches eight cards, they must immediately discard or play an Event card to return to at most seven.
answers.evidence: Actions, “Share Knowledge”: matching current-city card, same city, both agree; recipient exceeding 7 immediately discards or plays Event.

answers.answer: When sharing, the Researcher may give any City card from the Researcher’s hand to a player in the same city, on either player’s turn. This exception only transfers a card from the Researcher to the other player; another player cannot use it to give an arbitrary nonmatching City card to the Researcher.
answers.evidence: Roles, “Researcher”: any City card may be given to a player in same city; exception transfers from Researcher’s hand on either player’s turn and does not allow arbitrary cards given to Researcher.

answers.answer: After the actions, draw 2 Player cards together. If fewer than 2 cards remain when the draw is required, the players lose; do not reshuffle discards.
answers.evidence: Drawing Player Cards: “Draw the top 2 cards together”; fewer than 2 means game ends and players lose; do not reshuffle discards.

answers.answer: Resolve the Epidemic in order: (1) advance the Infection Rate marker 1 space; (2) draw the bottom Infection card and place cubes on its city. Since the city has two cubes of that color, add 1 to reach 3, then an outbreak occurs. Put the drawn Infection card on the Infection Discard Pile. (3) Reshuffle only the Infection Discard Pile and put it on top of the Infection Deck. Remove the Epidemic card from the game; do not draw a replacement Player card.
answers.evidence: Epidemic Cards: Increase, Infect (bottom card; add only enough to reach 3, then outbreak; discard Infection card), Intensify; remove Epidemic, no replacement.

answers.answer: After 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6 Epidemics, flip respectively 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, and 4 Infection cards per turn.
answers.evidence: Infection Rate Track table, “Epidemics Resolved” 0–6 and “Cards Flipped” 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, 4.

answers.answer: Resolve the first Epidemic’s three steps fully, then the second’s three steps fully; Events may be played between the two. First resolve any Epidemics drawn, then reduce an over-limit hand by discarding cards or playing Events until at most 7.
answers.evidence: Epidemic Cards: if two drawn at once, resolve all three steps for first then second; Events may be played between. Hand Limit: first resolve Epidemics, then discard/play Events to 7.

answers.answer: Flip Infection cards from the top of the Infection Deck, one at a time, equal to the current infection rate. For each non-eradicated disease, place 1 matching cube on the named city; a cured disease still places cubes if not eradicated. If the disease is eradicated, place no cube. If the city already has 3 cubes of that color, place no fourth cube and cause an outbreak. Put each Infection card in the Infection Discard Pile.
answers.evidence: Infecting Cities: top of deck/current infection rate; 1 cube unless eradicated; 3 cubes causes outbreak instead of 4th; discard each card. Cure Procedure says cured disease still infects until eradication.

answers.answer: For an outbreak, first advance the Outbreaks marker 1 space, then place 1 cube of that color in each city connected to the outbreak city. A connected city that already has 3 of that color causes a chain outbreak after the current outbreak resolves; advance the marker for each outbreak. During chain reactions for that Infection card, do not add cubes to cities that have already had an outbreak, so the chain does not spread back into the first city. The limit is 3 cubes per color per city; different colors may each have up to 3.
answers.evidence: Outbreaks steps: marker forward, spread to connected cities, chain after current outbreak resolves, no cubes to cities already outbreaking during current card; cities can have multiple colors up to 3 each.

answers.answer: No. Airlift cannot be played between drawing an Infection card and resolving it, so it cannot move the Quarantine Specialist before that outbreak. After resolving that card, an Event may be played before the next card is drawn/resolved. Any player may play Airlift at any time when not between drawing and resolving a card; it costs no action, and the player playing it chooses the use. Move any 1 pawn to any city (get permission for another player’s pawn), then discard Airlift to the Player Discard Pile.
answers.evidence: Event Cards: any player may play Events at any time, but not between drawing and resolving a card; player who plays decides use; discard to Player Discard Pile. Airlift effect; Events are not actions.

answers.answer: As an action, take 1 Event card from anywhere in the Player Discard Pile and store it on the Contingency Planner Role card. The storage limit is 1, and the stored Event does not count against the hand limit. When played, remove that Event from the game instead of discarding it.
answers.evidence: Roles, “Contingency Planner”: as action, take 1 Event from anywhere in Player Discard Pile, store on Role card, limit 1, not hand limit; on play remove from game.

answers.answer: The Dispatcher may spend an action to move any pawn to a city with another pawn, or move another player’s pawn as if it were their own; moving another player’s pawn requires the owner’s agreement. Direct/Charter Flight costs for directing another pawn are paid from the Dispatcher’s hand; for Charter Flight the card matches the moved pawn’s departure city. The Dispatcher may move another pawn but cannot make it Treat Disease or take other nonmovement actions. The Dispatcher cannot use the Operations Expert’s special move.
answers.evidence: Roles, “Dispatcher”: both movement options, owner agreement, Dispatcher pays Direct/Charter cards, Charter matches moved pawn’s departure, no nonmovement actions, cannot use Operations Expert move.

answers.answer: The team wins immediately when cures for all 4 diseases are discovered; eradication and a clear board are not required. The three losses are: the Outbreaks marker reaches the last space (8th outbreak); the needed disease cubes cannot be placed because the supply is exhausted (loss immediately during an epidemic, outbreak, or infection requiring cubes); or a player cannot draw 2 Player cards after actions because fewer than 2 remain.
answers.evidence: Victory; Defeat; Special Rules “Cube supply check”: inability to place needed cubes during epidemic, outbreak, or infection loses immediately.

answers.answer: Place the board within reach, with the 6 research stations and separated disease cubes nearby; put 1 station in Atlanta. Put the Outbreaks marker on 0 and the 4 cure markers vial-side up near the Discovered Cure Indicators. Give each player a Reference card; shuffle Role cards and deal 1 face up to each, place matching pawns in Atlanta, and remove unused Role cards and pawns. The player with the highest-population City card goes first.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1–5 and 9.

answers.answer: Teammates may offer advice, but the active player decides their actions. In Introductory games, play with cards face up for all to see. In Standard/Heroic, hands are private by default, though experienced groups may choose open hands. Anyone may inspect either discard pile at any time.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure; Special Rules, “Introductory game”: face-up; Standard/Heroic private by default, experienced groups may use open hands; anyone may examine either discard pile.

answers.answer: Removing the last cube of an uncured disease does not eradicate it or change its status. If the last cube of a cured disease is removed, eradicate it and flip its cure marker to the eradication side. After eradication, normal infections and Epidemics place no new cubes of that disease; before cure, the disease is not eradicated and may receive cubes.
answers.evidence: Eradication: last cube of cured disease means eradicated and flip marker; last cube of uncured disease has no effect; eradicated diseases receive no new cubes during infections or Epidemics.

answers.answer: The Epidemic’s Infect step places 3 cubes on that city because the disease is not eradicated and the city has zero cubes. There is no outbreak just for reaching 3; the summary says outbreak occurs if the city already has cubes of that color when Epidemic cubes are added. Put the Infection card on the Infection Discard Pile before Intensify.
answers.evidence: Epidemic Cards, Infect: place 3 unless eradicated; if city already has cubes, add only enough to reach 3, then outbreak; discard card to Infection Discard Pile.

answers.answer: Increase still happens: advance the Infection Rate marker by 1. The Infect step still draws the bottom Infection card, but places no cubes because the disease is eradicated; then discard that card to the Infection Discard Pile. Intensify still reshuffles only the Infection Discard Pile onto the top of the Infection Deck.
answers.evidence: Epidemic Cards: Increase; Infect draws bottom card, placement is “unless eradicated,” then discard; Intensify instruction.

answers.answer: After the first Epidemic’s Intensify, the Infection Discard Pile is empty. Thus the second bottom Infection card is the only card shuffled in the second Intensify, and it ends on top of the Infection Deck. The second Epidemic places 3 cubes in its city, since it starts at zero and is unprotected/non-eradicated. The next normal Infection draws that city first; it already has 3 cubes, so the Infection causes an outbreak.
answers.evidence: Two Epidemics at once note: second bottom card is the only card shuffled and ends on top; city brought to 3; drawn first during normal infections and causes outbreak.

answers.answer: The Scientist needs 4 same-color City cards instead of 5 to discover a cure. The player must still be at any research station, and the cards must still match the disease color; the station city’s color need not match.
answers.evidence: Cure Procedure: 4 for Scientist; at any research station; discard City cards of disease color; station city color need not match.

answers.answer: As an action, the Operations Expert builds a research station in the city they currently occupy. They do not need, use, or discard a City card.
answers.evidence: Roles, “Operations Expert”: as an action, build station in current city with no City card needed, used or discarded.

answers.answer: Once per turn, as an action, the Operations Expert may move from a research station to any city by discarding any City card. The card need not match the departure or destination city.
answers.evidence: Roles, “Operations Expert”: once per turn as an action, move from a research station to any city by discarding any City card.

answers.answer: One Treat Disease action by the Medic removes all cubes of one chosen color from the city, even when that disease is uncured. It does not remove other colors in that action; treating each different color takes a separate action.
answers.evidence: Roles, “Medic”: Treat Disease removes all cubes of one color; Actions: treat each different color with a separate action.

answers.answer: When the cure is discovered, if the Medic is already in a city with cubes of that color, remove all those cubes from that city immediately. Later, when another player moves the Medic into another city with cubes of the cured color via Dispatcher or Airlift on that player’s turn, the Medic automatically removes all cubes of that color from the city occupied or entered. The move was another player’s action/effect; the automatic removal itself costs no action.
answers.evidence: Roles, “Medic”: if already in city when cure discovered, remove its cubes immediately; entering via Dispatcher or Airlift on another player’s turn triggers automatic removal; cured-color cubes removed with no action needed.

answers.answer: The Medic prevents placement and outbreaks of cured diseases in the city the Medic occupies. This does not protect adjacent cities or uncured diseases.
answers.evidence: Roles, “Medic”: prevents placement and outbreaks of cured diseases in Medic’s city; no adjacent-city or uncured-disease protection.

answers.answer: The Quarantine Specialist prevents placement and outbreaks of every disease color in the city they occupy and all cities connected to it. This ability does not affect cubes placed during setup.
answers.evidence: Roles, “Quarantine Specialist”: all colors, current and connected cities; does not affect setup cubes.

answers.answer: Resilient Population removes any 1 card from the Infection Discard Pile from the game. It may be played between the Epidemic’s Infect and Intensify steps, so it can remove the Infection card just discarded in the Infect step before Intensify reshuffles the discard pile.
answers.evidence: Event Cards, “Resilient Population”: remove any 1 card in Infection Discard Pile from game; may play between Infect and Intensify.

answers.answer: One Quiet Night skips the next Infect Cities step, so no Infection cards are flipped for that step. It does not skip an Epidemic’s Infect step.
answers.evidence: Event Cards, “One Quiet Night”: skip next Infect Cities step and do not flip cards; does not skip an Epidemic’s Infect step.

answers.answer: Airlift moves any 1 pawn to any city. If moving another player’s pawn, get that player’s permission.
answers.evidence: Event Cards, “Airlift.”

answers.answer: Only Player cards count toward the 7-card hand limit. Role and Reference cards do not count, and an Event stored on the Contingency Planner Role card does not count. A hand of nine Player cards must be reduced by discarding cards or playing Event cards until it has at most seven (two cards’ worth), after first resolving any Epidemics just drawn.
answers.evidence: Hand Limit: Player cards only, max 7; role/reference do not count; over-limit reduction sequence. Contingency Planner stored Event does not count.

answers.answer: Government Grant places a research station in any city, whether or not the player is there, with no City card discard needed.
answers.evidence: Event Cards, “Government Grant”: place a research station in any city (no card discard needed).

answers.answer: Forecast lets you draw, view, and rearrange the top 6 cards of the Infection Deck, then put those cards back on top of that deck.
answers.evidence: Event Cards, “Forecast.”
